answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it can trade, so spawning a thousand sock-puppets means locking a thousand deposits, like trying to pave a dune with velvet — soft-looking, ruinously costly at scale. Misbehavior slashes the stake, so a sable-coated Sybil farm bleeds money faster than it earns, while honest agents keep trading and get their bond back.
